request.spec:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The tree search is in: a box and a button on the sheet list everyone in this sheet's tree whose name or alias contains the typed text, ignoring case. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

Each result line reads `<sheet id> <name> <due-total>`. This sheet's people come first in list order, then the other sheets' by sheet id. The due-total is the same figure the person's row shows, or `n/a`.

**Server:** a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree` (`rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree.GET.yml` and `sheet/RespondWithTree.java`), returns the ids of the other sheets in the tree, sorted. It reuses `PersonRepository.treeOf`, the same tree the rule that names must be unique across a tree already uses: parents going up and children going down.

**Front end:** the panel is in `features/search/search.slot.tsx`. It works like the consolidated-figures panel: it loads each sheet's people and claims and uses the existing due-total calculation. The test ids are `search-name`, `search`, `search-count` and `search-line`, plus `search-error` if the tree can't be read.

How it behaves in cases the spec doesn't cover:
- **Sibling sheets are left out.** The search covers the sheet's ancestors and descendants, not other branches under a shared parent. Claim numbering uses a wider tree (the top sheet and everything below it), so say if you want the search to use that one instead.
- **Retired people are included,** whether or not "show retired" is on, the same as the people export.
- **Each press reads every sheet fresh, as it stands now.** That means the results ignore any "as of" date the screen is set to, the same as the consolidated figures. The count stays blank until every sheet has been read.

probe.probe_text:
# Figures and rules in the sheet, as the code stands now Nothing was changed. I read the money logic myself: `Claim`, `Person`, `LateCharge`, `DatedSettings`, `Setting`, `Rollup`, `ApplyClaimStatus`, `ClaimStatus`, `ClaimRepository`, `SettleClaims`, and the front end's `useRates.ts`, `useClaims.ts` and the figure slots. Three read-only agents swept the ~350 other action classes. Their findings are marked † and I haven't checked each one line by line. ## 1a. Figures shown **Per claim** (`claim-row-`) - `claim-amount`, `claim-date`, `claim-note`, `claim-ref`, `claim-tags`, `claim-corrects`. - `claim-number`: `FY-` from the tree-wide fiscal sequence, or `-` / `X-` once `period-numbering-from` is reached (`ClaimNumbering`). - `claim-status`, `claim-opened-by`. - `claim-due`: computed in the front end by `claimDueCents`. - `claim-due-by`, `claim-overdue`, `claim-period` (the period containing the due-by), `claim-late-entry`. - `claim-deferred` / `claim-deferred-until`, `claim-proofs`, `claim-split-from`, `claim-reminded`, `claim-stated`, `claim-batch`, and the void reason. - `claim-log` (status lines ending `due=`), `claim-comments`, `claim-lines`. **Per person** (`person-row-`) - `person-claimed` - `person-due-total`, `person-settled-total`, `person-open-total`, `person-excess` - `person-overdue-count`, `person-overdue-total` - `person-aged-0-30`, `person-aged-31-60`, `person-aged-61` - `person-period-

-due-total`, `person-cut-total` - `person-active`, `person-backing`, `person-patrons` (shares) - `person-statement-count`, `person-stated-total`, `person-statement-date` - `person-grade`, `person-terms`, `person-retired-from`, `person-hold-*`, `person-clashing`, `person-snapshot-line` **Sheet** - `rollup-claimed-total`, `rollup-due-total`, `rollup-settled-total`, `rollup-open-total` - `rollup-overdue-count`, `rollup-overdue-total`, `rollup-cut-total` - `tag--due-total`, `month--due-total` - `period-due-total`, plus `period-closed` (yes / soft / no) and `period-cap` - The header counts, `header-due-total` / `header-overdue-total` and `my-due-total` / `my-overdue-total` - `consolidated-*` (the sheet plus its descendants) - Summary counts and totals per grade, period, status and void reason - `pool-total-share`, `pool-balanced`, `pool-cut`, `rate-current-`, `rate-preview-count` / `-diff` ## 1b. Rules that decide them **Which claims count** - `ClaimStatus.counts()`: OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED count. DRAFT, VOID and DELETED don't. - A claim is left out of every total when any of these applies: - **Deferral:** `isDeferredOn(today)`, meaning it is OPEN and deferred until a date after the sheet's today. - **Hold:** `Rollup.held`, meaning it is OPEN or PENDING, unbound, and either a hold covers its date or its person's `retiredOn(today)`. - `person-claimed` adds up amounts, leaving out corrections (claims that name `corrects`). **How a claim's due is worked out** (`LateCharge`, `Rollup.figure`, `claimDueCents`) 1. **Figure:** the `settledDue` if set. Else the `statedDue` while `isBound()` (stated and not PENDING). Else `figureAt`: amount × rate / 100. - The rate is the one in force on the claim's date for the person's `gradeOn(claim date)` (`Rate.on`). - The lookup tries the sheet's own rates, then its `parent` chain up to `PARENT_LEVELS = 3`. - A rate whose to-date has passed falls through to the parent; it doesn't fall back to an earlier rate on the same level. 2. **Rounding** (`LateCharge.rounding`): `HALF_UP` when `roundOn` is before `policy-date`, `HALF_EVEN` on or after it. A blank policy date means the sheet's today. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects. 3. **Late charge** (`onAsOpen`): - `lateFrom` = due-by + `grace-`. - For each full 30 days past `lateFrom`, it adds `late-pct` (as in force on that 30-day boundary) of (figure + the charge so far). This compounds, and each step is rounded. - There is no charge for corrections, deferred claims, or claims that aren't OPEN or PENDING. 4. **Floor:** the result is at least the `floor` in force on the claim's date (default 1.00). Corrections and settled claims get no floor. 5. **No rate means n/a.** **Per-person totals** - **Due-total:** the counting claims' dues added up, then held to at most the `cap` in force on today (`SettingRepository.capped`). - It shows **n/a** when today's grade has no rate today, unless something is "kept": a settled or bound figure, a figure at another grade, or a figure dated on or before today. - `person-excess` is the amount above the cap. - The settled and open totals split the uncapped total. - **Overdue** (`LateCharge.overdue`): OPEN or PENDING, and `lateFrom < today`. The overdue-total is uncapped. - **Sheet due and overdue totals** use `trimmed`: with three or more people, the single highest and lowest person are left out. Claimed, settled and open totals aren't trimmed. - **Aging buckets:** days from the claim's date to today, split 0–30, 31–60 and 61+. - **Active:** the person has a counting OPEN or PENDING claim dated in the last 30 days. - **Backing:** the patrons' SETTLED dues from the last 90 days × their share, rounded `HALF_EVEN`. - **Patron shares** (`getPatronShares`): 100.00 split equally, rounded `HALF_EVEN`, with the remainder going to the first patron named. **What is frozen, and when** - **Terms and due-by** are fixed when a claim is added. Terms come from `DatedSettings.terms(person, date)`: the person's own terms, else `terms-`, else the sheet's `terms` (default 14). - The due-by is the terms-th business day after the date, skipping weekends and holidays. - Re-dating or editing never moves the due-by. Adding a holiday re-fixes the due-by of later claims that aren't SETTLED or VOID (`ClaimRepository.refix`). - **Settling** freezes `settledDue` = figure + today's late charge, floored. A VOID-from-SETTLED claim keeps that frozen figure but counts nowhere. - **Resettle** (steward only†) recomputes the settled due. - **A statement** (`TakeStatement`†) binds each counting claim to its figure (`stated` / `statedDue`). - It records the person's capped due-total; `asOf` must be on or before today. - Split, reassign and `CancelStatement` (steward only) unbind. - The late charge and floor are never bound. - **Close or soft-close a period:** `closed_total` and each `period_person_total` are fixed (`dueBetweenByPerson`). - Claims count by due-by within the period, using their status at the end of `to` from the log. - A soft-close still allows changes, and claims added during it are marked `lateEntry`. - A closed period refuses any change whose due-by falls inside it (`RefuseClosed*`). - `ReopenPeriod` makes the totals live again. - `AutoClosePeriods`† closes periods past `to + grace-days` when today moves. It ignores permissions and skips soft-closed periods. **Who may do what** - **Roles:** `clerk` (the default), `steward`, `viewer`. A delegation acts as steward while the sheet's today is inside its window. - **`PERMISSION_STANDING`:** open, settle, void and close go to clerk and steward; reassign and reopen to steward only. `perm-` overrides these. - **Steward only:** review a PENDING claim (approve or reject with a reason), void a SETTLED claim within `VOID_SETTLED_DAYS = 7` of settling, plus† redate, resettle, cancel a statement, merge, transfer, archive and clone. - **Four-eyes:** neither `openedBy` nor `editedBy` may settle or approve the claim. - **Settle and open refusals:** - Settling above `proof-threshold[-grade]` without a proof is refused. - A clerk's settle above `clerk-limit` becomes **PENDING** instead. - Opening with an empty note above `note-threshold` is refused. - Opening beyond a period's `cap` of OPEN or PENDING claims is refused. - A deferred claim can't be settled. - If the sheet has void reasons, voiding needs one. - **Viewers, archived sheets and as-of views refuse changes.** Bulk actions don't raise an error: they report "0 done, all refused". - **Bulk settle** is all or nothing (`keepOnly`). **What a date decides** - **The sheet's today** drives the late charge, overdue, deferral, the retirement effect, the grade and cap in force, aging, the void window, and when a deleted claim can be restored (same day only). - **A blank date** on a new claim means `entry-date` if set, else today. A blank date on an edit means today†. - **Retirement:** - A claim dated after `retiredFrom`, or inside a past retirement, is refused. - From the retirement date, unbound live claims stop counting. - Bulk retire moves the date instead of refusing†. - **Holds** have no end action†. They exclude unbound live claims dated inside the hold. - **Imports**: - Importing people (†) adds new names or updates matching ones by name or alias. An update's grade is always given from today. - Importing rates writes one `RATE_SET` plus rollup lines per line. - Paste is all or nothing, with each line passing the same checks as an added claim. ## 2. How hard it was to follow It is scattered and tangled, not in one place a new developer could pick up. The due rule alone lives in at least three places that don't fully agree: - **Java `Rollup` / `LateCharge`:** these only feed the audit lines. - **A full TypeScript copy:** `useRates.ts` plus a dozen slot files actually compute every figure on screen. - **A third Java path in `TakeStatement` / `ApplyClaimStatus.dueNow`:** this uses `RateRepository.find`. Some of the copies already disagree: - The front end's `counts()` tests `stated` where the server tests `isBound()`. So a held, stated PENDING claim is counted on screen but not in the audit. - The front end looks up a correction's rounding date by claim number across all people; the server limits it to the same person. - Several comments describe old behaviour. The periods panel says "claims whose date falls in it", but the code uses the due-by. `ValidateClaimStatus` says only OPEN, SETTLED or VOID, but it also accepts DELETED and DRAFT. The rules are mostly written down only as long Javadoc comments, spread across hundreds of one-method OfficeFloor step classes and YAML pipelines. The access survey also turned up a likely gap. Any clerk can make anyone a steward (`roles.PUT`) and can change `perm-*`, `clerk-limit` and the sheet's today, because those endpoints only refuse viewers. That undoes every steward-only rule above.
